text: There is no one creature so obscure, so low, or so poor, who may not, by the strange and unaccountable changes and vicissitudes of human affairs, somehow or other, and some time or other, become an useful friend or a trouble-some enemy, to the greatest and the richest.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter CLXXXI, to his son, Bath, November 11, Old Style 1752
